answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the shale identifier and voids the later submissions, and thus the operator pays for 26 runs and collects one. Because the vine index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the ember audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 26 answers need 26 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
